* * *
Part of the **1985 Atlantic hurricane season**
**Hurricane Bob** was the first of six hurricanes to strike the United States during the 1985 Atlantic hurricane season. The second tropical storm and first hurricane of the year, Bob developed from a tropical wave on July 21 in the eastern Gulf of Mexico. Bob began moving east, making landfall southwestern Florida as a weak tropical storm. The storm then turned to the north and quickly intensified to hurricane status on July 24. The next day, it made landfall near Beaufort, South Carolina, becoming one of a record-tying six hurricanes to hit the United States during a single season.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-HURDAT-1) Bob quickly weakened over land, and was absorbed by a frontal trough over eastern West Virginia on July 26.
Bob caused $20 million in damage as well as five indirect deaths. In Florida, the storm produced heavy rainfall, peaking at over 20 inches (508 mm) in Everglades City. In most areas, the rainfall was beneficial due to dry conditions that had persisted throughout the year. Damage was minimal in South Carolina, where the hurricane made its final landfall. In Virginia, the storm spawned three tornadoes, one of which destroyed two houses.

## Meteorological history
[edit]
Map plotting the storm's track and intensity, according to the Saffir–Simpson scale
The remnants of a tropical wave entered the eastern Gulf of Mexico on July 20. An area of low pressure formed and developed into a tropical depression on July 21. Under weak steering currents, the tropical depression drifted southeast, then turned northeast and later east. Based on reports from Hurricane Hunters, the system intensified into Tropical Storm Bob late on July 22. Bob failed to organize significantly as it tracked east through the Gulf, and made landfall between Naples and Fort Myers, Florida, on July 23 as a 45 mph (70 km/h) tropical storm. At the time, most of the convection was concentrated south and east of the center.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-tcr1-2)

## Meteorological history
While moving across Florida, Bob turned to the northeast, then to the north. It subsequently left the peninsula, entering the Atlantic Ocean near Vero Beach early on July 24. As it moved over the warm waters of the Gulf Stream, it quickly organized and intensified into a Category 1 hurricane while 70 mi (115 km) east of Jacksonville, Florida.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-tcr1-2) Because it was embedded within the western extension of the subtropical ridge, Bob retained higher-than-average atmospheric pressures throughout its lifespan.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-mwr-3) The hurricane continued north, and made landfall near Beaufort, South Carolina, early on July 25 while maintaining winds of 75 mph (120 km/h). Bob quickly weakened over land, decaying into a tropical storm three hours after landfall.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-tcr1-2)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-tcr3-4) About 12 hours later, it degenerated into a tropical depression near the North Carolina – Virginia border. Bob's remnants turned north-northeast, and were absorbed by a frontal trough over eastern West Virginia on July 26.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-tcr1-2) An associated area of disturbed weather remained separate from the trough, and continued northeast through the Mid-Atlantic and New England.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-rain-5)

## Meteorological history
When Bob was designated a tropical storm, the National Hurricane Center issued gale warnings for the Florida Keys west of Craig Key, and from Flamingo to Venice. Gale warnings were later posted for the Atlantic coast of Florida northward through St. Augustine.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-tcr4-6) Small craft south of St. Augustine were advised to remain in port.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-flstuff-7) While the storm was situated off the east-central coast of Florida, the National Hurricane Center issued a gale warning and a hurricane watch from Savannah, Georgia, to Little River, South Carolina. The hurricane watch was upgraded to a hurricane warning after Bob's intensification to Category 1 status.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-tcr1-2)
Thousands of residents evacuated coastal areas of South Carolina, many of whom stayed at inland hotels; 850 people sought protection in shelters, including 500 at an elementary school in Horry County and 240 in a shelter in the Grand Strand. In Beaufort County, city and county offices were closed early and businesses were advised to send their workers home prematurely. Officials in Chatham County, Georgia, evacuated nursing homes on Tybee Island, and encouraged others to leave due to the potential for high tides to isolate the island by cutting off U.S. Route 80.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-scprep-8)
Hurricane Bob inflicted $20 million in damages[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-chap8-9) and caused five indirect deaths. Damage from the storm was not severe enough to justify retirement of the name "Bob", and as such it was re-used during the 1991 season.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-10)
Tropical Storm Bob making landfall on Florida

## Meteorological history
In southern Florida, the heaviest rainfall remained to the south and east of the storm's center; 21.5 inches (546 mm) of precipitation was recorded in Everglades City.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-mwr-3) Northern parts of the state reported trace amounts to several inches of precipitation.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-rain-5) At Naples, sustained winds reached 40 mph (65 km/h), with a peak gust of 58 mph (93 km/h).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-mwr-3) Rough surf and above-average tides caused moderate to severe beach erosion in portions of coastal Manatee, Sarasota, and Charlotte counties.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-erosion-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-surftides-12) Before landfall, Tropical Storm Bob spawned an F0 tornado in Brevard County that caused $2,500 in damage (1985 USD, $4,700 2006 USD) along its 1-mile (1.6 km) path.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-ehthsat-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-ncdcfl-14)

## Meteorological history
Tropical Storm Bob flooded roads and downed trees in Florida.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-swtb-15) Rough seas broke over sea walls in southwestern parts of the state, and the combination of high tides and heavy rain caused forced the closure of causeways to Sanibel Island and Marco Island, leaving the islands temporarily isolated. They were re-opened when the waters receded,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-flstuff-7) though the causeway to Sanibel Island sustained some damage.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-lcpd-16) Florida Power & Light Co. reported that 1,200 to 1,500 residences were without power on July 23.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-flstuff-7) In Palm Beach County, rainfall from the storm caused agricultural damage.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-pbc-17)
Overall damage was minimal and primarily confined to minor property near the coast. The storm's rainfall was beneficial in areas that had suffered dry conditions.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-flstuff-7) In northeastern Florida and Georgia, beach erosion occurred along the coast.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-mwr-3) Bob was one of four July tropical cyclones to affect Palm Beach County since 1878.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-apfourtc-18)
Estimated rainfall totals from Hurricane Bob

## Meteorological history
The strongest winds from Hurricane Bob were confined to areas east of its center when it came ashore around 1 am Eastern Standard Time (EST).[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-19) Along the barrier islands off the coast of Charleston, windows were broken and power lines knocked down. Further inland, the lack of damage in spite of high winds was described as "almost unbelievable".[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-20)Georgetown, South Carolina, 105 miles (170 km) northeast of where the storm made landfall, recorded sustained winds of 58 mph (93 km/h), and a spiral rainband produced a peak wind gust of 83 mph (134 km/h) in Holden Beach. Upon moving ashore, the hurricane produced an estimated storm tide of 2.6 feet (0.79 m) in Edisto Beach.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-mwr-3) Rainfall in the Carolinas was moderate; portions of coastal South Carolina received over 5 inches (127 mm) of precipitation.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-rain-5)Myrtle Beach reported a statewide peak of 7.79 inches (198 mm).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-mwr-3) Hurricane-force wind gusts downed trees and power lines, leaving over 32,000 people without power, including more than 25,000 in the Charleston area. Near the coast, high winds shattered windows.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-scdam-21)

## Meteorological history
Strong waves broke over sea walls in Charleston, spilling floodwaters onto coastal streets and homes.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-bobupi-22) Damage in the state was relatively light, and no serious injuries were reported.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-scdam-21) However, a gas station in Folly Beach was torn apart by the winds,[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-23) and some structures along the coast sustained roof damage.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-24) In the Charleston Harbor, an empty tanker was forced aground on a sandbar by the winds.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-25) Throughout most areas, the storm was insignificant; a police sergeant in Summerville commented, "All we've had were some trees blown over, hardly enough to make it worth staying up so late."[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-26)
Much of North Carolina received over 1 inch (25.4 mm) of rain; as much as 7 inches (178 mm) fell in Beaufort County.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-rain-5) The storm caused one traffic-related fatality in the state.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-tcr2-27)

## Meteorological history
### Mid-Atlantic and New England
[edit]
In Virginia, a large band of thunderstorms associated with the hurricane brought strong winds and spawned three tornadoes. A funnel cloud formed in Albemarle County evolved into an F3 tornado after crossing into Greene County. It destroyed two houses and uprooted several trees,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-vaem-28) inflicting $250,000 in damage (1985 USD, $470,000 2006 USD).[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-ncdcva-29) F0 tornadoes were also generated in Goochland County and Hanover County;[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-vaem-28) the two tornadoes damaged a total of ten houses. Funnel clouds were sighted throughout the Baltimore-Washington Metropolitan Area.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-virhis-30)
Heavy precipitation and high winds disrupted the 1985 Boy Scouts of AmericaNational Scout Jamboree at Fort A. P.

## What happened with Bob
**Hurricane Bob (1985)** was a **Category 1 hurricane** of the 1985 Atlantic season. It formed on July 21, 1985, 175 mi WSW of Venice, Florida, reached its peak of **75 mph (120 km/h)** and a minimum pressure of **1002 mb** on July 24, 1985, and made landfall 14 mi E of Hilton Head Island, South Carolina on July 25, 1985 as a Category 1 hurricane (75 mph). The storm lasted 4.8 days and travelled about 1,136 miles (1,828 km).

## What happened with Bob
**Hurricane Bob (1985)** was a **Category 1 hurricane** of the 1985 Atlantic season. It formed on July 21, 1985, 175 mi WSW of Venice, Florida, reached its peak of **75 mph (120 km/h)** and a minimum pressure of **1002 mb** on July 24, 1985, and made landfall 14 mi E of Hilton Head Island, South Carolina on July 25, 1985 as a Category 1 hurricane (75 mph). The storm lasted 4.8 days and travelled about 1,136 miles (1,828 km).

* * *
Part of the **1985 Atlantic hurricane season**
**Hurricane Bob** was the first of six hurricanes to strike the United States during the 1985 Atlantic hurricane season. The second tropical storm and first hurricane of the year, Bob developed from a tropical wave on July 21 in the eastern Gulf of Mexico. Bob began moving east, making landfall southwestern Florida as a weak tropical storm. The storm then turned to the north and quickly intensified to hurricane status on July 24. The next day, it made landfall near Beaufort, South Carolina, becoming one of a record-tying six hurricanes to hit the United States during a single season.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-HURDAT-1) Bob quickly weakened over land, and was absorbed by a frontal trough over eastern West Virginia on July 26.
Bob caused $20 million in damage as well as five indirect deaths. In Florida, the storm produced heavy rainfall, peaking at over 20 inches (508 mm) in Everglades City. In most areas, the rainfall was beneficial due to dry conditions that had persisted throughout the year. Damage was minimal in South Carolina, where the hurricane made its final landfall. In Virginia, the storm spawned three tornadoes, one of which destroyed two houses.
texts.1:
## Meteorological history
[edit]
Map plotting the storm's track and intensity, according to the Saffir–Simpson scale
The remnants of a tropical wave entered the eastern Gulf of Mexico on July 20. An area of low pressure formed and developed into a tropical depression on July 21. Under weak steering currents, the tropical depression drifted southeast, then turned northeast and later east. Based on reports from Hurricane Hunters, the system intensified into Tropical Storm Bob late on July 22. Bob failed to organize significantly as it tracked east through the Gulf, and made landfall between Naples and Fort Myers, Florida, on July 23 as a 45 mph (70 km/h) tropical storm. At the time, most of the convection was concentrated south and east of the center.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-tcr1-2)
texts.2:
## Meteorological history
While moving across Florida, Bob turned to the northeast, then to the north. It subsequently left the peninsula, entering the Atlantic Ocean near Vero Beach early on July 24. As it moved over the warm waters of the Gulf Stream, it quickly organized and intensified into a Category 1 hurricane while 70 mi (115 km) east of Jacksonville, Florida.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-tcr1-2) Because it was embedded within the western extension of the subtropical ridge, Bob retained higher-than-average atmospheric pressures throughout its lifespan.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-mwr-3) The hurricane continued north, and made landfall near Beaufort, South Carolina, early on July 25 while maintaining winds of 75 mph (120 km/h). Bob quickly weakened over land, decaying into a tropical storm three hours after landfall.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-tcr1-2)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-tcr3-4) About 12 hours later, it degenerated into a tropical depression near the North Carolina – Virginia border. Bob's remnants turned north-northeast, and were absorbed by a frontal trough over eastern West Virginia on July 26.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-tcr1-2) An associated area of disturbed weather remained separate from the trough, and continued northeast through the Mid-Atlantic and New England.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-rain-5)
texts.3:
## Meteorological history
When Bob was designated a tropical storm, the National Hurricane Center issued gale warnings for the Florida Keys west of Craig Key, and from Flamingo to Venice. Gale warnings were later posted for the Atlantic coast of Florida northward through St. Augustine.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-tcr4-6) Small craft south of St. Augustine were advised to remain in port.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-flstuff-7) While the storm was situated off the east-central coast of Florida, the National Hurricane Center issued a gale warning and a hurricane watch from Savannah, Georgia, to Little River, South Carolina. The hurricane watch was upgraded to a hurricane warning after Bob's intensification to Category 1 status.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-tcr1-2)
Thousands of residents evacuated coastal areas of South Carolina, many of whom stayed at inland hotels; 850 people sought protection in shelters, including 500 at an elementary school in Horry County and 240 in a shelter in the Grand Strand. In Beaufort County, city and county offices were closed early and businesses were advised to send their workers home prematurely. Officials in Chatham County, Georgia, evacuated nursing homes on Tybee Island, and encouraged others to leave due to the potential for high tides to isolate the island by cutting off U.S. Route 80.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-scprep-8)
Hurricane Bob inflicted $20 million in damages[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-chap8-9) and caused five indirect deaths. Damage from the storm was not severe enough to justify retirement of the name "Bob", and as such it was re-used during the 1991 season.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-10)
Tropical Storm Bob making landfall on Florida
texts.4:
## Meteorological history
In southern Florida, the heaviest rainfall remained to the south and east of the storm's center; 21.5 inches (546 mm) of precipitation was recorded in Everglades City.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-mwr-3) Northern parts of the state reported trace amounts to several inches of precipitation.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-rain-5) At Naples, sustained winds reached 40 mph (65 km/h), with a peak gust of 58 mph (93 km/h).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-mwr-3) Rough surf and above-average tides caused moderate to severe beach erosion in portions of coastal Manatee, Sarasota, and Charlotte counties.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-erosion-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-surftides-12) Before landfall, Tropical Storm Bob spawned an F0 tornado in Brevard County that caused $2,500 in damage (1985 USD, $4,700 2006 USD) along its 1-mile (1.6 km) path.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-ehthsat-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-ncdcfl-14)
texts.5:
## Meteorological history
Tropical Storm Bob flooded roads and downed trees in Florida.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-swtb-15) Rough seas broke over sea walls in southwestern parts of the state, and the combination of high tides and heavy rain caused forced the closure of causeways to Sanibel Island and Marco Island, leaving the islands temporarily isolated. They were re-opened when the waters receded,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-flstuff-7) though the causeway to Sanibel Island sustained some damage.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-lcpd-16) Florida Power & Light Co. reported that 1,200 to 1,500 residences were without power on July 23.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-flstuff-7) In Palm Beach County, rainfall from the storm caused agricultural damage.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-pbc-17)
Overall damage was minimal and primarily confined to minor property near the coast. The storm's rainfall was beneficial in areas that had suffered dry conditions.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-flstuff-7) In northeastern Florida and Georgia, beach erosion occurred along the coast.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-mwr-3) Bob was one of four July tropical cyclones to affect Palm Beach County since 1878.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-apfourtc-18)
Estimated rainfall totals from Hurricane Bob
texts.6:
## Meteorological history
The strongest winds from Hurricane Bob were confined to areas east of its center when it came ashore around 1 am Eastern Standard Time (EST).[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-19) Along the barrier islands off the coast of Charleston, windows were broken and power lines knocked down. Further inland, the lack of damage in spite of high winds was described as "almost unbelievable".[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-20)Georgetown, South Carolina, 105 miles (170 km) northeast of where the storm made landfall, recorded sustained winds of 58 mph (93 km/h), and a spiral rainband produced a peak wind gust of 83 mph (134 km/h) in Holden Beach. Upon moving ashore, the hurricane produced an estimated storm tide of 2.6 feet (0.79 m) in Edisto Beach.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-mwr-3) Rainfall in the Carolinas was moderate; portions of coastal South Carolina received over 5 inches (127 mm) of precipitation.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-rain-5)Myrtle Beach reported a statewide peak of 7.79 inches (198 mm).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-mwr-3) Hurricane-force wind gusts downed trees and power lines, leaving over 32,000 people without power, including more than 25,000 in the Charleston area. Near the coast, high winds shattered windows.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-scdam-21)
texts.7:
## Meteorological history
Strong waves broke over sea walls in Charleston, spilling floodwaters onto coastal streets and homes.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-bobupi-22) Damage in the state was relatively light, and no serious injuries were reported.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-scdam-21) However, a gas station in Folly Beach was torn apart by the winds,[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-23) and some structures along the coast sustained roof damage.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-24) In the Charleston Harbor, an empty tanker was forced aground on a sandbar by the winds.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-25) Throughout most areas, the storm was insignificant; a police sergeant in Summerville commented, "All we've had were some trees blown over, hardly enough to make it worth staying up so late."[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-26)
Much of North Carolina received over 1 inch (25.4 mm) of rain; as much as 7 inches (178 mm) fell in Beaufort County.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-rain-5) The storm caused one traffic-related fatality in the state.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-tcr2-27)
texts.8:
## Meteorological history
### Mid-Atlantic and New England
[edit]
In Virginia, a large band of thunderstorms associated with the hurricane brought strong winds and spawned three tornadoes. A funnel cloud formed in Albemarle County evolved into an F3 tornado after crossing into Greene County. It destroyed two houses and uprooted several trees,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-vaem-28) inflicting $250,000 in damage (1985 USD, $470,000 2006 USD).[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-ncdcva-29) F0 tornadoes were also generated in Goochland County and Hanover County;[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-vaem-28) the two tornadoes damaged a total of ten houses. Funnel clouds were sighted throughout the Baltimore-Washington Metropolitan Area.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-virhis-30)
Heavy precipitation and high winds disrupted the 1985 Boy Scouts of AmericaNational Scout Jamboree at Fort A. P.

## What happened
Bob crossed southwest Florida between Naples and Fort Myers as a tropical storm on July 23, 1985.1It then came ashore on the South Carolina coast near Beaufort, at Fripp Island, at 0300 UTC on July 25 (11 p.m. EDT on July 24) as a minimal Category 1 hurricane with 65-knot (75 mph) winds and a 1003 mb pressure.1,2,3
Rain totaled up to 21.5 inches in 48 hours at Everglades City, Florida, and 6 to 8 inches over parts of the Carolinas.4Charleston Airport received 5 inches of rain, and gusts reached 44 mph in downtown Charleston and 48 mph at Folly Beach.5The highest gust NHC reported was 72 knots (83 mph) at Holden Beach, North Carolina.1The tide at Charleston Harbor peaked at 6.6 feet above mean low water, and NHC estimated the storm surge at 3 to 5 feet above normal.4NHC attributed one traffic death in North Carolina to Bob and rated the damage as minor.4

* * *
Part of the **1985 Atlantic hurricane season**
**Hurricane Bob** was the first of six hurricanes to strike the United States during the 1985 Atlantic hurricane season. The second tropical storm and first hurricane of the year, Bob developed from a tropical wave on July 21 in the eastern Gulf of Mexico. Bob began moving east, making landfall southwestern Florida as a weak tropical storm. The storm then turned to the north and quickly intensified to hurricane status on July 24. The next day, it made landfall near Beaufort, South Carolina, becoming one of a record-tying six hurricanes to hit the United States during a single season.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-HURDAT-1) Bob quickly weakened over land, and was absorbed by a frontal trough over eastern West Virginia on July 26.
Bob caused $20 million in damage as well as five indirect deaths. In Florida, the storm produced heavy rainfall, peaking at over 20 inches (508 mm) in Everglades City. In most areas, the rainfall was beneficial due to dry conditions that had persisted throughout the year. Damage was minimal in South Carolina, where the hurricane made its final landfall. In Virginia, the storm spawned three tornadoes, one of which destroyed two houses.

## Meteorological history
[edit]
Map plotting the storm's track and intensity, according to the Saffir–Simpson scale
The remnants of a tropical wave entered the eastern Gulf of Mexico on July 20. An area of low pressure formed and developed into a tropical depression on July 21. Under weak steering currents, the tropical depression drifted southeast, then turned northeast and later east. Based on reports from Hurricane Hunters, the system intensified into Tropical Storm Bob late on July 22. Bob failed to organize significantly as it tracked east through the Gulf, and made landfall between Naples and Fort Myers, Florida, on July 23 as a 45 mph (70 km/h) tropical storm. At the time, most of the convection was concentrated south and east of the center.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-tcr1-2)

## Meteorological history
While moving across Florida, Bob turned to the northeast, then to the north. It subsequently left the peninsula, entering the Atlantic Ocean near Vero Beach early on July 24. As it moved over the warm waters of the Gulf Stream, it quickly organized and intensified into a Category 1 hurricane while 70 mi (115 km) east of Jacksonville, Florida.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-tcr1-2) Because it was embedded within the western extension of the subtropical ridge, Bob retained higher-than-average atmospheric pressures throughout its lifespan.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-mwr-3) The hurricane continued north, and made landfall near Beaufort, South Carolina, early on July 25 while maintaining winds of 75 mph (120 km/h). Bob quickly weakened over land, decaying into a tropical storm three hours after landfall.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-tcr1-2)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-tcr3-4) About 12 hours later, it degenerated into a tropical depression near the North Carolina – Virginia border. Bob's remnants turned north-northeast, and were absorbed by a frontal trough over eastern West Virginia on July 26.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-tcr1-2) An associated area of disturbed weather remained separate from the trough, and continued northeast through the Mid-Atlantic and New England.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-rain-5)

## Meteorological history
When Bob was designated a tropical storm, the National Hurricane Center issued gale warnings for the Florida Keys west of Craig Key, and from Flamingo to Venice. Gale warnings were later posted for the Atlantic coast of Florida northward through St. Augustine.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-tcr4-6) Small craft south of St. Augustine were advised to remain in port.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-flstuff-7) While the storm was situated off the east-central coast of Florida, the National Hurricane Center issued a gale warning and a hurricane watch from Savannah, Georgia, to Little River, South Carolina. The hurricane watch was upgraded to a hurricane warning after Bob's intensification to Category 1 status.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-tcr1-2)
Thousands of residents evacuated coastal areas of South Carolina, many of whom stayed at inland hotels; 850 people sought protection in shelters, including 500 at an elementary school in Horry County and 240 in a shelter in the Grand Strand. In Beaufort County, city and county offices were closed early and businesses were advised to send their workers home prematurely. Officials in Chatham County, Georgia, evacuated nursing homes on Tybee Island, and encouraged others to leave due to the potential for high tides to isolate the island by cutting off U.S. Route 80.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-scprep-8)
Hurricane Bob inflicted $20 million in damages[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-chap8-9) and caused five indirect deaths. Damage from the storm was not severe enough to justify retirement of the name "Bob", and as such it was re-used during the 1991 season.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-10)
Tropical Storm Bob making landfall on Florida

## Meteorological history
In southern Florida, the heaviest rainfall remained to the south and east of the storm's center; 21.5 inches (546 mm) of precipitation was recorded in Everglades City.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-mwr-3) Northern parts of the state reported trace amounts to several inches of precipitation.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-rain-5) At Naples, sustained winds reached 40 mph (65 km/h), with a peak gust of 58 mph (93 km/h).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-mwr-3) Rough surf and above-average tides caused moderate to severe beach erosion in portions of coastal Manatee, Sarasota, and Charlotte counties.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-erosion-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-surftides-12) Before landfall, Tropical Storm Bob spawned an F0 tornado in Brevard County that caused $2,500 in damage (1985 USD, $4,700 2006 USD) along its 1-mile (1.6 km) path.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-ehthsat-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-ncdcfl-14)

## Meteorological history
Tropical Storm Bob flooded roads and downed trees in Florida.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-swtb-15) Rough seas broke over sea walls in southwestern parts of the state, and the combination of high tides and heavy rain caused forced the closure of causeways to Sanibel Island and Marco Island, leaving the islands temporarily isolated. They were re-opened when the waters receded,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-flstuff-7) though the causeway to Sanibel Island sustained some damage.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-lcpd-16) Florida Power & Light Co. reported that 1,200 to 1,500 residences were without power on July 23.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-flstuff-7) In Palm Beach County, rainfall from the storm caused agricultural damage.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-pbc-17)
Overall damage was minimal and primarily confined to minor property near the coast. The storm's rainfall was beneficial in areas that had suffered dry conditions.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-flstuff-7) In northeastern Florida and Georgia, beach erosion occurred along the coast.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-mwr-3) Bob was one of four July tropical cyclones to affect Palm Beach County since 1878.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-apfourtc-18)
Estimated rainfall totals from Hurricane Bob

## Meteorological history
The strongest winds from Hurricane Bob were confined to areas east of its center when it came ashore around 1 am Eastern Standard Time (EST).[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-19) Along the barrier islands off the coast of Charleston, windows were broken and power lines knocked down. Further inland, the lack of damage in spite of high winds was described as "almost unbelievable".[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-20)Georgetown, South Carolina, 105 miles (170 km) northeast of where the storm made landfall, recorded sustained winds of 58 mph (93 km/h), and a spiral rainband produced a peak wind gust of 83 mph (134 km/h) in Holden Beach. Upon moving ashore, the hurricane produced an estimated storm tide of 2.6 feet (0.79 m) in Edisto Beach.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-mwr-3) Rainfall in the Carolinas was moderate; portions of coastal South Carolina received over 5 inches (127 mm) of precipitation.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-rain-5)Myrtle Beach reported a statewide peak of 7.79 inches (198 mm).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-mwr-3) Hurricane-force wind gusts downed trees and power lines, leaving over 32,000 people without power, including more than 25,000 in the Charleston area. Near the coast, high winds shattered windows.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-scdam-21)

## Meteorological history
Strong waves broke over sea walls in Charleston, spilling floodwaters onto coastal streets and homes.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-bobupi-22) Damage in the state was relatively light, and no serious injuries were reported.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-scdam-21) However, a gas station in Folly Beach was torn apart by the winds,[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-23) and some structures along the coast sustained roof damage.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-24) In the Charleston Harbor, an empty tanker was forced aground on a sandbar by the winds.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-25) Throughout most areas, the storm was insignificant; a police sergeant in Summerville commented, "All we've had were some trees blown over, hardly enough to make it worth staying up so late."[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-26)
Much of North Carolina received over 1 inch (25.4 mm) of rain; as much as 7 inches (178 mm) fell in Beaufort County.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-rain-5) The storm caused one traffic-related fatality in the state.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-tcr2-27)

## Meteorological history
### Mid-Atlantic and New England
[edit]
In Virginia, a large band of thunderstorms associated with the hurricane brought strong winds and spawned three tornadoes. A funnel cloud formed in Albemarle County evolved into an F3 tornado after crossing into Greene County. It destroyed two houses and uprooted several trees,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-vaem-28) inflicting $250,000 in damage (1985 USD, $470,000 2006 USD).[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-ncdcva-29) F0 tornadoes were also generated in Goochland County and Hanover County;[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-vaem-28) the two tornadoes damaged a total of ten houses. Funnel clouds were sighted throughout the Baltimore-Washington Metropolitan Area.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Bob_(1985)#cite_note-virhis-30)
Heavy precipitation and high winds disrupted the 1985 Boy Scouts of AmericaNational Scout Jamboree at Fort A. P.

Title: Hurricane Floyd battering Carolinas
Chunks: 0,1,2
NEWS
Bruce Smith
The Herald Times
Sept. 16, 1999, 1:00 a.m. ET
MYRTLE BEACH, S.C. — The leading edge of Hurricane Floyd knocked out power, flooded streets with drenching rain and spun off tornadoes Wednesday night as the Carolinas braced for a direct hit from the storm.Its howling winds reduced to a still-dangerous 115 mph, Floyd moved north toward the mostly evacuated area between Myrtle Beach and Wilmington, N.C., after delivering only a glancing blow to Florida and Georgia earlier in the day.Altogether, authorities have urged more than 2.6 million people along the southern Atlantic coast to clear out of Floyd\'s path — the biggest peacetime evacuation in U.S. history.At 10 p.m. Bloomington time, Floyd was 100 miles south-southwest of Wilmington. The storm\'s center was moving north-northeast at 18 mph and was expected to roll ashore before daybreak today with a storm surge 7 to 11 feet above normal tide levels.By nightfall Wednesday, hurricane-strength gusts of 80 mph had buffeted Charleston, S.C., and more than 200,000 people in the area lost power. Winds gusted to near tropical storm strength and several tornadoes struck near Wilmington.Earlier, in northern and central Florida, Floyd snapped power lines, smashed piers into driftwood and knocked out electricity to 300,000 people. About 350 miles off the coast, the Navy and Coast Guard rescued eight people whose tugboat sank in 30-foot seas churned up by the hurricane.But Floyd made a northward turn that spared Florida and Georgia the catastrophic damage many had feared. NASA\'s Kennedy Space Center and its four shuttles were largely unscathed.The Carolinas, however, lay directly in the storm\'s path."I know that Florida and Georgia at this point feel like they\'ve dodged a real bullet," said North Carolina\'s public safety secretary, Richard Moore. "This thing is not going to miss us."Myrtle Beach, a usually bustling resort, was a virtual ghost town as people fled or stayed indoors, and highways were jammed around Wilmington.

In both Carolinas, many hurricane-hardened people who rode out earlier storms left this time.Terry Hurley, checking into a Wilmington shelter with his wife and two children, said his family stayed home for Hurricanes Fran and Bertha in 1996, but not for Floyd."They talk like this one is going to be pretty mean," he said. "It\'s got everybody shook up."Myrtle Beach authorities imposed a 3 p.m. curfew and turned off the water supply. The hospital sent its patients inland but kept a doctor and three nurses on emergency duty.South Carolina Gov. Jim Hodges banned price gouging on essential items, threatening fines up to $100 or 30 days in jail. "All of us — no matter what our means — deserve the same access to lifesaving food and supplies," he said.The last time South Carolina took a direct hit from a major hurricane was almost exactly 10 years ago, when Hugo struck near Charleston with 135 mph winds. The storm killed 29 people and caused $5.9 billion in damage, the most costly hurricane to hit the U.S. mainland until Hurricane Andrew hit Florida in 1992.Floyd weakened slightly Wednesday to a Category 3 storm, its winds down from a peak of nearly 155 mph when it battered the Bahamas. The storm\'s hurricane-force winds extended 140 miles from its center.Floyd\'s expected track would take its wind and rain up through the mid-Atlantic states and into New England and Canada by Saturday night. Forecasters said Floyd could still have winds over 50 mph when it hits Maine.In Beaufort County, at South Carolina\'s southern tip, an estimated 90 percent of its nearly 120,000 residents heeded the call to evacuate."It\'s like a tomb out here now," said Bud Boyne, a county emergency spokesman.North Carolina authorities issued evacuation orders for the barrier islands outside Wilmington and for the Outer Banks, the fragile line of islands that were battered by a lingering Hurricane Dennis last week.President Clinton, hurrying back from New Zealand to deal with the hurricane, pre-emptively declared federal disaster areas in South Carolina and North Carolina.

He had issued similar declarations Tuesday for Florida and Georgia to allow a rapid start to any recovery efforts."I think we\'ve done everything we know to do," Clinton said.Hundreds of airline flights in and out of Florida and Georgia were canceled, and Amtrak suspended all train service south of Washington.Walt Disney World remained closed Wednesday, the second day of its first weather-related shutdown in its 28-year history. But SeaWorld reopened and scheduled a "Farewell to Floyd" fireworks show.Although Floyd stayed off Florida\'s Atlantic coast Tuesday night and Wednesday morning, parts of the state were raked by winds of more than 75 mph. A weather buoy more than 20 miles off Cape Canaveral measured a 54-foot wave as Floyd\'s eye passed over during the night.The sea sheared off the end of the Jacksonville Pier and swallowed about 100 feet of the century-old Daytona Beach pier."It just kept trying to go for about 10 minutes and then a big wave just pulled it in," said Calvin Williams, 42, a dishwasher at a restaurant near the Daytona Beach pier. "A lot of people clapped and yelled when it fell. I didn\'t think that was called for. The tears came to my eyes because this is a nice beach."Floyd\'s early strength had raised fears of a repeat of Hurricane Andrew, which smashed into South Florida with 145 mph winds, killing 26 people and causing an estimated $25 billion in damage.

NEWS

The Herald Times
Sept. 16, 1999, 1:00 a.m. ET
MYRTLE BEACH, S.C. — The leading edge of Hurricane Floyd knocked out power, flooded streets with drenching rain and spun off tornadoes Wednesday night as the Carolinas braced for a direct hit from the storm.Its howling winds reduced to a still-dangerous 115 mph, Floyd moved north toward the mostly evacuated area between Myrtle Beach and Wilmington, N.C., after delivering only a glancing blow to Florida and Georgia earlier in the day.Altogether, authorities have urged more than 2.6 million people along the southern Atlantic coast to clear out of Floyd\'s path — the biggest peacetime evacuation in U.S. history.At 10 p.m. Bloomington time, Floyd was 100 miles south-southwest of Wilmington. The storm\'s center was moving north-northeast at 18 mph and was expected to roll ashore before daybreak today with a storm surge 7 to 11 feet above normal tide levels.By nightfall Wednesday, hurricane-strength gusts of 80 mph had buffeted Charleston, S.C., and more than 200,000 people in the area lost power. Winds gusted to near tropical storm strength and several tornadoes struck near Wilmington.Earlier, in northern and central Florida, Floyd snapped power lines, smashed piers into driftwood and knocked out electricity to 300,000 people. About 350 miles off the coast, the Navy and Coast Guard rescued eight people whose tugboat sank in 30-foot seas churned up by the hurricane.But Floyd made a northward turn that spared Florida and Georgia the catastrophic damage many had feared. NASA\'s Kennedy Space Center and its four shuttles were largely unscathed.The Carolinas, however, lay directly in the storm\'s path."I know that Florida and Georgia at this point feel like they\'ve dodged a real bullet," said North Carolina\'s public safety secretary, Richard Moore. "This thing is not going to miss us."Myrtle Beach, a usually bustling resort, was a virtual ghost town as people fled or stayed indoors, and highways were jammed around Wilmington.
texts.1: In both Carolinas, many hurricane-hardened people who rode out earlier storms left this time.Terry Hurley, checking into a Wilmington shelter with his wife and two children, said his family stayed home for Hurricanes Fran and Bertha in 1996, but not for Floyd."They talk like this one is going to be pretty mean," he said. "It\'s got everybody shook up."Myrtle Beach authorities imposed a 3 p.m. curfew and turned off the water supply. The hospital sent its patients inland but kept a doctor and three nurses on emergency duty.South Carolina Gov. Jim Hodges banned price gouging on essential items, threatening fines up to $100 or 30 days in jail. "All of us — no matter what our means — deserve the same access to lifesaving food and supplies," he said.The last time South Carolina took a direct hit from a major hurricane was almost exactly 10 years ago, when Hugo struck near Charleston with 135 mph winds. The storm killed 29 people and caused $5.9 billion in damage, the most costly hurricane to hit the U.S. mainland until Hurricane Andrew hit Florida in 1992.Floyd weakened slightly Wednesday to a Category 3 storm, its winds down from a peak of nearly 155 mph when it battered the Bahamas. The storm\'s hurricane-force winds extended 140 miles from its center.Floyd\'s expected track would take its wind and rain up through the mid-Atlantic states and into New England and Canada by Saturday night. Forecasters said Floyd could still have winds over 50 mph when it hits Maine.In Beaufort County, at South Carolina\'s southern tip, an estimated 90 percent of its nearly 120,000 residents heeded the call to evacuate."It\'s like a tomb out here now," said Bud Boyne, a county emergency spokesman.North Carolina authorities issued evacuation orders for the barrier islands outside Wilmington and for the Outer Banks, the fragile line of islands that were battered by a lingering Hurricane Dennis last week.President Clinton, hurrying back from New Zealand to deal with the hurricane, pre-emptively declared federal disaster areas in South Carolina and North Carolina.
texts.2: He had issued similar declarations Tuesday for Florida and Georgia to allow a rapid start to any recovery efforts."I think we\'ve done everything we know to do," Clinton said.Hundreds of airline flights in and out of Florida and Georgia were canceled, and Amtrak suspended all train service south of Washington.Walt Disney World remained closed Wednesday, the second day of its first weather-related shutdown in its 28-year history. But SeaWorld reopened and scheduled a "Farewell to Floyd" fireworks show.Although Floyd stayed off Florida\'s Atlantic coast Tuesday night and Wednesday morning, parts of the state were raked by winds of more than 75 mph. A weather buoy more than 20 miles off Cape Canaveral measured a 54-foot wave as Floyd\'s eye passed over during the night.The sea sheared off the end of the Jacksonville Pier and swallowed about 100 feet of the century-old Daytona Beach pier."It just kept trying to go for about 10 minutes and then a big wave just pulled it in," said Calvin Williams, 42, a dishwasher at a restaurant near the Daytona Beach pier. "A lot of people clapped and yelled when it fell. I didn\'t think that was called for. The tears came to my eyes because this is a nice beach."Floyd\'s early strength had raised fears of a repeat of Hurricane Andrew, which smashed into South Florida with 145 mph winds, killing 26 people and causing an estimated $25 billion in damage.

## Answer

Out of all tropical cyclones whose storm tracks passed within 15 nautical miles (~17.3 statute miles) of Myrtle Beach, SC between 1953 and 2023, **two cyclones produced maximum rainfall of at least 15 inches somewhere in the contiguous United States**:

### 1. **Hurricane Florence (2018)** ✓
- **Storm Track:** Became a tropical storm over eastern South Carolina "just north of Myrtle Beach" (September 14-15, 2018). The storm's center passed extremely close to the Myrtle Beach area during this period.
- **Maximum Rainfall in CONUS:** 23.63 inches near **Loris, South Carolina** (within ~15 miles of Myrtle Beach), with isolated amounts up to 30-40 inches across portions of eastern North and South Carolina.

### 2. **Hurricane Floyd (1999)** ✓
- **Storm Track:** The storm's eye passed "just offshore of the Myrtle Beach area" in the early morning hours of September 16, 1999, bringing hurricane-force winds to coastal Myrtle Beach.
- **Maximum Rainfall in CONUS:** 16.80 inches at **Myrtle Beach International Airport**, with **North Myrtle Beach Airport recording 16.06 inches**. Additionally, Southport, NC recorded 24.06 inches (the highest in the country for this storm).
